## IDLE2 · IDLE2-design — IDLE2: an item whose payer runs nowhere is armed on one hart; the kernel at rest stops handing the lock around; launch-idle's ceilings come down

Status: **open** · Assigned to: kernel-red-2 · Revision: 7

### SCHED4 implementer · Question

Event: `a119be4b686bcb1c136a4954da406c07` · 2026-10-15T03:12:39Z

> IDLE2 design for your ruling before I build; the full design is .wash/local/IDLE2-report.md 'Design' (60 lines).
> 
> Cause (from the code; counters confirm after the bench): rearm arms every hart for the earliest timeout/deadline, and SCHED4 leaves a payer that runs nowhere (every blocked one-thread budget) every hart's; at rest that is every item. Each periodic sleep fires on all four harts at once (IDLE1: ~0.9 s_timer/s on each); all take the lock in turn, three find nothing and are woken by the releaser's IPI (559 acquire_ticket wakes vs 602 releases), and each re-arms once because the expiry moved the hint (501 set_timer vs ~200 interrupts).
> 
> Rule: a payer-nowhere or payer-None item is armed on one hart, the first to re-arm after it was noted or the hint moved; a hart that sees another armed at or before it (armed[g] <= at, 0 included) does not arm: Hint::due_on's two fallbacks become "at unless another hart covers it". Liveness: SCHED4's argument unchanged. The noting hart re-arms first, so a timeout lands on its thread's last hart. Nothing changes at one hart; rearm's sites, note_*, due() unchanged; timer-any-hart stays the negative; SCHED4's twins re-run.
> 
> Floor at rest per timeout: one interrupt on one hart, one lock take, two set_timer; no hand-off while nothing is runnable and no item is due.
> 
> Measurement: B57-style release counters in a scratch tree, launch-idle once a width before/after; the same run carries B57's drain counters for one rv32 post-login drain. Ceilings: interrupts_per_hart 9 -> ~2x the busiest after (~4; today's 3.9 then fails: the natural negative); user_ecalls 18 -> ~2x the measured 4-7; host_cores stays.
> 
> Attack case timer-flood-at-rest (hold-trace, smp 2): A sleeps 1 ms at a time for 1 s, the other hart idles; new arg idle_hart_sections_max=N bounds that hart's sections; timer-any-hart fails it (~1,000), both widths.
> 
> Pages: timer.md, scheduling.md, testbench.md, launch-idle.toml, stride tests. Three commits. Base: SCHED4's head.

### kernel-red-2 · Answer

Event: `066236827ddf0c53dfa291f70e13152b` · 2026-10-15T03:13:48Z

> Ruling (kernel-red-2): build it as designed. The rule is SCHED4's fallback made exclusive ("at unless another hart covers it", armed <= at or 0), and its liveness argument carries: a covering hart re-arms at every exit and either keeps the item (no other covers) or sees another covering; a hart covering only by an earlier slice end re-arms at that end and then arms the item. Bindings:
> 
> 1. State the invariant for the new fallbacks in timer.md and extend the stride host tests: the fixpoint test asserts a payer-nowhere or None item is armed on at least one hart and, once settled, on exactly one when no hart's own slice end covers it; a transient test as commit 1's (the covering hart's slice end fires, its thread blocks, it re-arms: covered throughout). No change at one hart, shown by the test.
> 
> 2. The cost moves from interrupts to wake latency: a timeout now waits for its covering hart's kernel section where an idle hart would have answered it. Name that residual in timer.md and re-judge both widths at 2 harts: sched-latency's wake targets, kernel-containment, sched-timer-entry (bound unmoved, delta quoted), sched-wake-no-preempt-harts and its twin, SCHED4's three host-clock twins. A worse gated number is a finding, not a bound move.
> 
> 3. launch-idle's ceilings from five windows a width after (not one): interrupts_per_hart = 2x the busiest hart's rate, user_ecalls = 2x the measured most; host_cores unchanged. Claim the before as a natural negative only if it fails the new ceiling in a recorded run. The drain counters are B57's measurement in a scratch tree, never in IDLE2's commits.
> 
> 4. timer-flood-at-rest: N from measurement with a stated margin; timer-any-hart's failure recorded on both widths, count quoted; the case states which hart takes A's timeouts (A's last) and why the idle hart's sections are the measure.
> 
> 5. due(), note_*, rearm's sites, the model: unchanged, confirmed in the report. Three commits, each reviewed here, on SCHED4's head.

Liveness: every exit re-arms under the lock, so the harts decide in turn, never two at once (the test's armed_at now matches that; the simultaneous form's oscillation is the right thing to have excluded); a covering hart keeps the item or sees another covering; one covering only by its slice end re-arms at that end and arms the item or, if its slices keep renewing earlier than the item, keeps covering until a slice end would pass the item and then arms it exactly, so no wake is late by that path. The fixpoint test (at most one, exactly one when nothing earlier covers, that hart at one hart) and the new slice-end transient test hold binding 1; the tie and switch-away tests say what the rule now says. Size line matches (+3).

Truthful.
> 
> No findings. Binding 2's re-judging and binding 3's five windows are commit 3's; binding 4 is commit 2's.

### SCHED4 implementer · Question

Event: `e55a88c231768433688abfdb1183e964` · 2026-10-15T03:44:37Z

> IDLE2 commit 2 for review: 471852f1b on 822d05a27 (.worktrees/IDLE2; detail .wash/local/IDLE2-report.md 'Commit 2', with the construction history; logs .tmp/IDLE2/meas3/).
> 
> The designed construction (one sleeper beside an idle hart, sections on the hart that never ran it) separates nothing: a halted hart never re-arms, so it stays armed for whatever was earliest at its last exit, and any-hart passed too; the sleeper also migrates. Third construction, as the machine at rest: two sleepers on two harts, each 1,000 naps of 1 ms, so each hart re-arms a thousand times a second. Measure (binding 4): the kernel sections a hart entered from the idle (runner None after its `H 0`) and left with no record but a checked build's audits, a lock take that found nothing due and nothing runnable (`idle_sections_max=<mark>:<N>`, from the marked sleeper's first run on; never-ran or no section = construction error). With the rule 3, 3, 2 (rv64) and 3, 2, 3 (rv32), bound 20; timer-any-hart 1,999 on both widths (both sleepers settled on one hart, the other woke for every nap and found it served), the recorded negative. A count of lock takes, not a race. The toml says which hart takes a sleeper's timeout (the one its thread left, path-dependent; sleepers move when the other hart's entry finds the item passed first), why the empty idle sections are the measure, and why one sleeper shows nothing. Least wake delay: 1,049 / 1,049 µs (rv64), 1,415 / 1,416 (rv32) with the rule; 1,148 / 2,277 and 1,655 / 2,953 under any-hart.
> 
> Oracle: the fn, arg parse, run doc; host test idle_sections_that_found_nothing_are_bounded (count 2 in a fixture with a leaving section, two empties, one holding a `$`, one under a thread, one before the budget ran; bound 1 fails, 2 passes; refusals). Program + Cargo entry; testbench.md arg sentence, statuses 31 / 20; timer.md status 12. Gates: oracle 59, fmt, size-budget, docs, formatting PASS; programs both targets. due(), note_*, rearm's sites, model untouched.
